info.title: GoodVibes Operator API
info.description: Generated from the operator contract (packages/contracts/artifacts/operator-contract.json). 636 cataloged methods: 529 with dedicated REST bindings, 107 reachable only through the generic invoke endpoint. Regenerate with `bun run openapi:generate`; drift fails `contracts:check`.

get.description: Return provider account posture.

post.description: Approve a pending approval. Optionally pass selectedHunks (edit-tool approvals only): the daemon filters the approval's own edit list to those hunk indices server-side, so every surface produces identical modified-edit args. Omitting selectedHunks approves the whole request (back-compat). An out-of-range index or a non-edit approval is rejected with a 400. rememberTier generalizes the decision (a generalizing tier persists a durable rule and sweeps queued asks it covers); modifiedArgs carries an argument-modifying approval, e.g. the typed answer to a command's terminal prompt, to the waiting call (selectedHunks supersedes it when both are present). The response's recorded block reports what the broker actually recorded. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal` naming its state (still 200, so a raced or retried decision does not fail).

Cancel a pending approval. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal` naming its state. A surface that raised the ask through approvals.raise and is leaving passes `release: true`: the ask is cancelled only when no other surface that raised the same ask is still waiting, otherwise it stays pending for them and the response reads `applied: false`. Pass the `holdId` that approvals.raise returned so a retried release is harmless instead of giving up another surface's hold.

Claim a pending approval for operator handling. A claim is advisory: it shows who is handling the ask and does not stop another participant from deciding it. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal`.

Deny a pending approval. rememberTier generalizes the denial (a generalizing tier persists a durable deny rule and sweeps queued asks it covers); reason is the user's free-text feedback, which rides the structured declined result so the model adapts instead of guessing. The response's recorded block reports what the broker actually recorded. An approval that already ended is returned unchanged with `applied: false` and a `refusal` naming its state (still 200, so a raced or retried decision does not fail).

get.description: Return pending and historical approval records, newest 50. Pass `approvalId` to read one record by id wherever it ranks; `approvals` then holds that record, or is empty when the id is unknown.
Return the raw content bytes for a stored artifact.

post.description: Store a file or attachment artifact for later delivery, analysis, or knowledge ingest. JSON supports small inline bodies and daemon-local path/URI references; HTTP callers can also send multipart/form-data or a raw binary body for large uploads.

get.description: Return stored artifact metadata for files and attachments.
Return metadata for a stored artifact.

Revoke a local auth session.

post.description: Create a local auth user. roles: omitted creates an admin. scopes: the operator scopes the user holds (for example read:sessions, read:transcripts and write:sessions for someone who only chats); omitted, the user holds its role's default set. A narrowed user is not an admin, whatever its roles.

delete.description: Delete a local auth user.

post.description: Rotate a local auth user password.

Give a local auth user a narrower list of operator scopes, or return it to its role's default set with scopes: null. Takes effect on the user's next request. An unknown user is 400; a scopes value that is neither a nonempty list nor null is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming scopes.

get.description: Return automation jobs queued for the next heartbeat.

post.description: Process automation jobs queued for the next heartbeat.

get.description: Return the automation integration snapshot.

post.description: Create a durable automation job. An optional id keeps the job under that id and makes the create repeatable: when a job with that id already exists it is returned unchanged.

get.description: Return automation jobs and recent runs. Without ?limit/?cursor returns { jobs: [...] } (backward compatible). With ?limit=N (1–500, default 100) and optional ?cursor=<opaque> returns a PaginatedResponse envelope { items, hasMore, nextCursor? }. Invalid cursors return HTTP 400.

delete.description: Delete a durable automation job.

patch.description: Update a durable automation job. (Renamed from automation.jobs.patch in the 1.0.0 core-verb rename, canonical verb is update, not patch.)

post.description: Disable a durable automation job.
Enable a durable automation job.
Trigger an automation job immediately.
Cancel an active automation run.

get.description: Return a single automation run record.

Return automation run history. Without ?limit/?cursor returns { runs: [...] } (backward compatible). With ?limit=N (1–500, default 100) and optional ?cursor=<opaque> returns a PaginatedResponse envelope { items, hasMore, nextCursor? }. Invalid cursors return HTTP 400. Optional ?since=<epoch-ms> returns only runs active on or after that time (by queuedAt, or endedAt when set), the host-side source an away-digest reads to report the failed, missed, completed, and delivered runs since the operator was last present.

post.description: Retry a completed or failed automation run.
Create a schedule record.

get.description: Return schedule records.

defaultTimezone.description: The IANA zone a cron schedule created without a timezone is stored in: the host's own zone.

delete.description: Delete a schedule record.

post.description: Disable a schedule record.
Enable a schedule record.
Trigger a schedule immediately.

Cancel a queued job. A job already in a terminal state is returned unchanged; a job already submitted to the provider is refused with 409 BATCH_JOB_ALREADY_SUBMITTED, because provider batches cancel as a whole: the refusal names the provider batch and `next` points at batch.providerBatches.cancel. Needs an admin.

Queue one chat request to run later as part of a provider batch, answered 202 with the queued job. A message or tool the provider could never accept is refused here with INVALID_BATCH_REQUEST rather than accepted with a job id. `flush: true` submits it right away instead of waiting for the next pass, and the response then carries the job as that pass left it. When the provider cannot batch (no batch API, or not configured for it) and `batch.fallback` is `live`, the request runs at once on the live path and the job comes back finished: `completed` with its result, or `failed` with code LIVE_FALLBACK_FAILED, marked `metadata["goodvibes.execution"] = "live-fallback"`; with `fallback: fail` it is refused with BATCH_PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED or BATCH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED (409). Refused with BATCH_DISABLED (409) while the mode is `off`, LIVE_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED (400) for `executionMode: "live"`, and BATCH_REQUEST_TOO_LARGE (413) above the request size limit. Spends provider budget, so it needs an admin.

get.description: Batch jobs, newest first. `limit` defaults to 100 and is capped at 1000.
One batch job with its status and, once finished, its result or error. An unknown id is a 404 with code BATCH_JOB_NOT_FOUND.

post.description: Cancel a whole provider batch at the provider (the `providerBatchId` shown on a submitted job) and mark its jobs. `providerStatus` is what the provider answered: `cancelled` when it stopped, `running` while it is still winding down, in which case requests it finished before the cancel are collected by the next pass and the rest are marked cancelled when it ends. `jobs` is every job of that batch as the cancel left it. A batch whose jobs are all finished is returned unchanged. Refused with BATCH_PROVIDER_BATCH_NOT_FOUND (404) when no job belongs to the id and BATCH_PROVIDER_CANCEL_UNSUPPORTED (409) when the provider has no cancel call. Needs an admin.

Run one submit-and-poll pass over the queue now instead of waiting for the timer. `force: true` submits queued jobs even before their delay has elapsed. Returns the counts for this pass, all zero when the mode is `off`. Spends provider budget, so it needs an admin.

get.description: The batch queue's current mode (`off`: nothing is queued; `explicit`: the job API is open and a non-streaming OpenAI-compatible chat completion is queued when it sends `x-goodvibes-execution: batch`; `eligible-by-default`: every such completion whose provider can batch is queued unless it sends `x-goodvibes-execution: live`, and one whose provider cannot runs live as usual), what happens to a job whose provider cannot batch (`fallback`: `live` runs it at once on the live path and answers it finished, `fail` refuses it), which queue backend holds jobs, the Cloudflare settings it would use, its limits, and the providers that can batch. `GET /api/batch` and `GET /api/batch/config` return the same document.

post.description: Click an element resolved from the latest snapshot of this page. Activating a control that submits a form is an outward effect and is refused when this turn has read untrusted page content.

Read named fields out of elements matched by a snapshot ref or a CSS selector. The function that runs in the page is fixed and ships in the engine; there is no way to express code here. Password input values are never returned.
Move the page back one entry in its history.
Move the page forward one entry in its history.
Load a URL, opening a session first if none is open. http, https, file and about schemes only; a javascript: URL is refused because it runs script against whatever page is already loaded.
Send one key to an element resolved from the latest snapshot. Enter is treated as a form submission and is an outward effect.
Install the browser driver and binary this machine needs, reporting each step it actually ran. Slow on a clean machine; every other verb provisions on demand.
Read the page as text, including open shadow roots and embedded frames, each frame origin recorded separately. Returns the text inside an untrusted-content envelope.
Write a PNG of the visible area or the whole scrollable page and report the exact path written.
Scroll the page by an amount, or bring a snapshot element into view.
Choose option values in a select element resolved from the latest snapshot.

Connect to a browser already running at a remote debugging endpoint on this machine (a bare port, localhost or a loopback address; a browser elsewhere is reached through a local port forward). The daemon can drive it but can never close it.
End a browser the daemon started. A session attached to a browser the daemon did not start is refused; release it instead.
Start a browser the daemon owns. Pass a profileName to keep sign-ins across runs; headless defaults to true where no display exists.

get.description: Return every open browser session, including whether the daemon started it and may therefore close it.

post.description: Disconnect from a session and leave the browser running. This is how an attached browser is let go of.
Return addressable element refs for the current page. Element names come from the page, so the result is untrusted content and is labelled as such.

get.description: Report whether a browser is available on this machine, where its binary came from, whether a display exists, and which sessions are open.

post.description: Close one tab. The browser itself keeps running.
Open a new tab, optionally at a URL, opening a session first if none is open.

get.description: Return every open page in a session, with which one is active.

post.description: Make another open tab the active one for later page verbs.
Type into an element resolved from the latest snapshot. There is no variant that types into whatever window has focus. submit:true presses Enter afterwards and is an outward effect.
Wait for text to become visible, for the URL to match, or for the network to settle. The timeout bounds this call only and never ends the browser.

get.description: The calendars the configured account can reach (the Google calendar list, or the CalDAV collections), so a client can offer them as choices and setup can offer them for surfaces.calendar.defaultCalendarId. A backend that cannot discover calendars answers 501 CALENDAR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

post.description: Create an event on the configured calendar. Requires explicit confirmation (confirm: true); attendees are invited by the calendar. Change it with calendar.events.update and remove it with calendar.events.delete.

get.description: Return event summaries from the configured calendar (a CalDAV server, or the connected Google account) within an optional time window. With no from or to, lists from 24 hours ago to 30 days ahead; a recurring event is listed at each occurrence in the window.

delete.description: Remove an event from the configured calendar (Google or CalDAV). Requires explicit confirmation (confirm: true). `deleted: false` means the calendar no longer held it. A whole recurring series is refused with 409 CALENDAR_SERIES_NOT_SUPPORTED (on Google, one occurrence is removed by the id calendar.events.list gives it); an event that changed after it was read is refused with 409 CALENDAR_EVENT_CHANGED. A backend that cannot delete events answers 501 CALENDAR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

get.description: Return the full event object including attendees, recurrence, and raw iCalendar UID.

patch.description: Change an event on the configured calendar (Google or CalDAV): only the fields sent change (attendees replaces the guest list; start and end are both dates for an all-day event or both date-times). Requires explicit confirmation (confirm: true). An unknown eventId is a 404; an id that names a whole recurring series is refused with 409 CALENDAR_SERIES_NOT_SUPPORTED (on Google, one occurrence is changed by the id calendar.events.list gives it); an event that changed on the calendar after it was read is refused with 409 CALENDAR_EVENT_CHANGED and nothing is written. A backend that cannot change events answers 501 CALENDAR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

get.description: Export events from the configured calendar as raw .ics content within an optional time window. With no limit every event in the window is exported; with a limit the export stops there and more: true says the window holds further events.

post.description: Import raw .ics content into the configured calendar. Requires explicit confirmation (confirm: true). A series and its overrides are stored together as written; an event already on the calendar is kept unless replace: true. Guests an imported event names are not invited; they are listed in attendeesLeftOff.

Run a lifecycle action on a specific channel account.

Return channel account lifecycle posture.

Return LLM agent tools for a single channel surface.

Resolve allowlist candidates into stable channel identities.
Evaluate channel authorization and availability for a requested action.

Return capability posture for a single surface.
Query a channel directory surface for users, groups, threads, or services.
Return doctor checks and repair posture for a channel surface.

delete.description: Remove a channel draft from the daemon-side store.

get.description: Return one channel draft by id: the owner (admin) receives its text, so a draft written on one device can be finished and sent on another; any other caller receives the redacted record. Webhook values stay redacted. An id that names no draft returns a notFound marker.

Return channel drafts for cross-device sync, metadata only: each message reads as a redacted marker and webhook values are redacted. The daemon is the store of record; the text is served by channels.drafts.get.

post.description: Mirror a channel draft to the daemon-side store. Webhook values must be redacted before transmission; raw webhook tokens are rejected. Requires explicit confirmation; a call made with the Agent's credential (the Agent acting on the owner's behalf) instead takes fresh recorded native admission.

Write triage labels to inbox messages at their provider: an IMAP keyword on mail, a reaction on Slack, a reaction or forum tag on Discord. `itemIds` are ids from channels.inbox.list (up to 100); `labels` are GoodVibes/Spam, GoodVibes/Priority or GoodVibes/Normal (writing one takes the other two off), or a custom label name. Writes only for accounts whose owner switch is on (surfaces.slack.inboxTagging, surfaces.discord.inboxTagging, surfaces.email.inboxTagging). Returns one result per message: `applied` (every label is on it now), `refused` (nothing was written, with the reason and what to do) or `failed` (the provider did not take a label; `effects` says which mark was written or not).

get.description: Return the merged inbound message feed (Slack DMs, Discord messages, email threads) from the host's synced provider mirror, newest first. Read-only; no provider write. Every known provider reports its own state in `providers`, including the unconfigured and the failing ones, so a short list is never ambiguous, and `partial` is true whenever a configured provider's items are missing because its last sync failed. Page with ?limit and ?cursor (opaque, from nextCursor); ?since=<cursor> returns only items committed after a previous answer's `cursor` watermark (the store's commit sequence, not a time); ?provider=<id> narrows to one provider; `uids` (a list of mail UIDs) returns only those messages of the live mailbox, matched by the email provider's current account and mailbox generation, so a client can look up a listed page without reading the feed. Each provider with triage says in `triage` whether new messages are being labelled and, when not, why and what turns it on; channels.inbox.triage labels a page now. An email item says in `screening` whether privacy screening read its text: `not-screened` (with `screeningReason`) when only code checked it for credential and card text; its subject is always the sender's own.

post.description: Score a page of one provider's stored inbox now: each message gets a spam / priority / normal label from the decision model on the account's privacy-screening route (labels otherwise come after each poll, so this is for a backlog or a re-check). `provider` is required (slack, discord or email); page with `limit` (at most 100) and `cursor` (nextCursor from channels.inbox.list or an earlier answer). `dryRun: true` returns the readings without storing them. Returns one receipt per message: `settled` with its label and score, or `held` / `unavailable` / `withheld` with why nothing was settled. When triage is off for the account the call is refused with the reason and what turns it on; channels.inbox.list reports the same state on each provider as `triage`.

get.description: Return lifecycle version posture for a channel surface.
Return channel ingress policy audit records.
Return ingress policy configuration for channels.

post.description: Update ingress policy configuration for a channel surface.

delete.description: Remove a channel profile binding. Returns { deleted: false } when no binding for that key existed, an honest boolean, never a phantom removal.

get.description: Return the profile binding for a channel (surfaceKind plus optional channelId) and `effective`: what a session that channel originates gets, each field merged from this binding and the surface-wide one, with `sources` naming the binding id that supplied each field. Returns 404 when no binding for that exact key exists. A listed or returned binding with `invalid` holds a value this build cannot use; that field is left out until the binding is set again or deleted.

Return every per-channel profile binding: the model, provider and permission-mode defaults the daemon applies to the sessions each channel originates. These are the values that apply; a channels.routing assignment for the same channel names a profile that only the surface owning it resolves.

post.description: Bind (upsert) the model/provider and permission-mode defaults for a channel. Keyed on (surfaceKind, channelId?): field by field, a channelId-scoped binding wins over the surface-wide default; setting the same key again replaces it. A session the daemon originates from the channel uses these values whatever a channels.routing assignment names.

get.description: Return repair actions exposed by a channel surface.

post.description: Create or update a channel-to-profile routing rule in the daemon-persisted routing table. The daemon applies it on every channel surface (slack, discord, telegram, msteams and the rest) and to slack, discord and email inbox items: an agent started for a message from the channel takes the profile's model and reasoning effort when neither the request nor the channel profile chose a model. routeId is the conversation (a chat, channel or room id); without it the rule covers the whole surface, and surfaceKind any covers every channel. tui, web and service are refused with 400 ROUTING_SURFACE_NOT_ROUTED, because their model is chosen in the surface itself. Requires explicit confirmation; a call made with the Agent's credential (the Agent acting on the owner's behalf) instead takes fresh recorded native admission.

get.description: Return the daemon-persisted channel-to-profile routing table. The profileId a rule names is stamped on inbox items from that channel (their routeId) so the surface owning the profile picks them up; it sets no model, provider or permission mode. Those come from channels.profiles.*, the one table the daemon applies to sessions a channel originates.

delete.description: Remove a channel-to-profile routing rule from the daemon-persisted routing table.

get.description: Return the versioned setup schema, secret targets, and external steps for a channel surface.
Return status for channel plugins and provider-backed channels.

post.description: Resolve a typed channel target for outbound delivery or routing.
Run a channel-owned operator tool.

get.description: Return operator tools registered by channel plugins.
Return operator tools for a single channel surface.

post.description: Stop the running turn of a Home Assistant chat session, named by sessionId or by a known messageId. The session stays open. A session that is not a Home Assistant chat session answers 404.

get.description: Report whether the Home Assistant surface is enabled and the conversation endpoints it serves.

post.description: Post one utterance and stream the reply as server-sent events: delta frames, then one final or error frame. A providerId or modelId of the caller's choosing needs an admin token.

Post one utterance to the isolated chat session of a Home Assistant conversation and wait for the reply (or return at once with wait false). A providerId or modelId of the caller's choosing needs an admin token. A tools list is refused.

get.description: Return the proactive check-in configuration (enabled, cadence (cron), delivery channel, quiet hours) and `schedule`: whether the scheduler really holds the check-in job (scheduled), none is needed (not-needed: check-ins are off), or it could not be installed (failed, with the reason; for example the automation subsystem is off). Enabled with a failed schedule means no check-in will arrive.

post.description: Update the proactive check-in configuration. Absent fields are left unchanged. Enabling syncs the kind:checkin automation job onto the scheduler; disabling stops it. The answer carries `schedule` (scheduled, not-needed, or failed with the reason), because the config is stored even when the scheduler could not install the job.

get.description: Return the visible receipts of past check-in runs (newest first): each run records whether it stayed quiet, delivered a message (and what), or was skipped.

post.description: Trigger one check-in evaluation immediately (a manual run): assemble the briefing, judge whether to contact the user, deliver if so, and record a receipt.

Poll GitHub for a repo/ref/PR and return EVERY job with its conclusion. The overall verdict is derived from the per-job conclusions (never a rollup); continue-on-error jobs are surfaced as violations and force the verdict off "passed".

Create a standing watch on a repo/ref or PR. On a terminal verdict it notifies the channel. Failed jobs request a fresh recorded repair decision from the original source owner; the compatibility flag is not authorization.

get.description: Return every standing CI watch, each with `expiresAt` (when it ends without a verdict) and, after a repair was tried for the current failure, `repair` (its outcome, attempts and next retry). Stored flags are not repair authority; production repair requires current original-source ownership and Jev admission.

delete.description: Remove a standing CI watch. Returns { deleted: false } when no watch with that id existed.

post.description: Poll a standing watch immediately: returns the per-job report, whether a completion notification fired, and whether an admitted fix-session started, or an honest refusal/error. When the check ended the watch without a verdict or a repair, `retired` is true and `endedReason` says why.

Check that the API token (inline, by reference, or the stored one) is valid and return the account it belongs to. A missing token is refused with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_REQUIRED (400) and a token Cloudflare rejects fails the call with Cloudflare's error. Changes nothing.

Switch the Cloudflare integration off. Always disables it locally (`cloudflare.enabled` false and the batch queue back to `local`; `persistConfig` defaults to true) and stops this daemon's tunnel connector, so the daemon stops using the worker. When an API token and account are available it also removes the worker's daemon credential (the script secret and its Secrets Store copy), its cron trigger (`disableCron`, default true) and its workers.dev route (`disableWorkerSubdomain`, default true; pass false to keep the route). `remote` is `disabled` only when every Cloudflare step succeeded; otherwise it is `not-disabled`, the deployed worker may keep calling the daemon until it is disabled in the Cloudflare dashboard, and `steps` says which. The worker and the account's other resources stay in place; each one still deployed is listed as a `still-deployed` step. With `bootstrapToken` (a token allowed to edit API tokens) it also revokes the operational token this daemon created; without it a `revoke-operational-token` step says that token is still live.

Create or update the selected Cloudflare resources (worker, queues and dead-letter queue, tunnel and its connector on this daemon, Access application and service token, DNS records, KV for queued-job state, Durable Objects for the daily queue budget, R2 for job bodies, Secrets Store for the worker's credentials), answered 202 with one step per resource: `ok`, `skipped` or `warning`; `warnings` repeats the message of every warning step. Generated secrets are stored as `goodvibes://` secrets when asked and returned only when `returnGeneratedSecrets` is true. With Workers selected and a worker URL known it then runs the `cloudflare.worker.verify` check unless `verify` is false. `ok` is true, and `cloudflare.enabled` and the Cloudflare batch queue are switched on, only when that check passed (or was turned off) and Access, when asked for, protects the daemon hostname; otherwise a `switch-on` warning step says why nothing was switched. Creates and changes billable resources in the Cloudflare account.

List what the account already has for the selected components: accounts, zones, the workers.dev subdomain and, with `includeResources`, existing queues, KV namespaces, Durable Object namespaces, R2 buckets, Secrets Stores, tunnels and Access applications. Read-only against Cloudflare; sent as a POST so credentials and the component selection travel in the body.

get.description: Whether the Cloudflare control plane is enabled and ready, which of its settings and credentials are configured (booleans only, never values), the stored non-secret configuration, and the warnings that explain anything missing. A resource (worker, queues, tunnel, Access, KV, Durable Objects, R2, Secrets Store) reads as configured only when a provision created or confirmed it at Cloudflare. Where this daemon runs the Cloudflare Tunnel connector, `tunnelConnector` says whether it is connected and what to do when it is not; `ready` requires it. `GET /api/cloudflare` returns the same document.

post.description: Use a temporary bootstrap token (required, used once, never stored) to create a narrower operational token with the permissions `cloudflare.token.requirements.get` lists. With `storeApiToken` the operational token is saved as a `goodvibes://` secret and its reference is returned; the plaintext token comes back only when `returnGeneratedToken` is true. When this daemon already holds the operational token it made for the same account, zone and components, that token is returned with `reused` true and nothing is created (`reuse: false` makes a new one). A new token revokes the one it replaces; `replaced` says whether that worked. Answered 201. Creates a credential in the Cloudflare account unless one is reused.

The Cloudflare API permissions each selected component needs, and how to create the one-off bootstrap token that `cloudflare.token.create` uses. Components default to Workers and Queues. Reads nothing from Cloudflare and changes nothing. Sent as a POST so the component selection travels in the body.

Check the deployed worker: its `/batch/health` route (`workerHealth`) and its `/api/batch/config` proxy to this daemon (`daemonBatchProxy`), each with `ok`, the HTTP status and any error; `ok` is true only when both pass. A stored worker client token is sent only to the configured `cloudflare.workerBaseUrl`; for any other URL pass `workerClientToken` in the request or the proxy check reports why it was not authenticated. The URL must be https and is required (CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL_REQUIRED, 400). Changes nothing.

get.description: Server-Sent Events stream of turn and agent events scoped to a single companion-chat session.

200.description: A server-sent event stream. Each event carries a JSON payload; the connection stays open until the client closes it.

post.description: Post a user message to a companion-chat session. Accepts either `body` or `content` in the payload; `body` wins when both are provided. Attachments reference artifacts created through `artifacts.create`. A message queued behind a running turn whose turn can never run (the chat closed, the service shut down or the daemon restarted first) ends as `deliveryState: "unanswered"`. Optional `clientMessageId` (1-128 characters) makes the send safe to repeat: a second send with the same id returns the first message's id and starts no second turn, so a client whose response was lost can resend. The id is remembered while the session stays loaded in the daemon; a daemon restart forgets it.

get.description: Return the messages of a companion-chat session, oldest first. With neither `limit` nor `before` the whole transcript is returned. With `limit` (1-1000, default 100 when only `before` is given) and/or `before` (a message id) one page is returned: the messages just before `before`, or the newest ones. Every answer carries `total` and `more`; while `more` is true, pass `nextBefore` back as `before` to read the page before it. A `before` that names no message in the chat is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND.

post.summary: Edit Companion Chat Message And Branch
post.description: Edit a user message and branch the conversation from it. `messageId` (required) is the user message to edit; the edited text is passed as `body` or `content` (as message create accepts), with optional `attachments` referencing artifacts. The original message and everything after it are SUPERSEDED, retained as history, never deleted, a new user message carrying `revisionOf` back to the original is appended, and a fresh turn answers it. Returns the new message id and the superseded ids for honest lineage. Same closed/unknown-session refusals as companion.chat.messages.retry, and the same 409 CHAT_TURN_BUSY while a reply, a message being prepared, or queued sends are in flight (nothing is superseded).

Regenerate an assistant response. Omitted `messageId`: the latest answered user message is answered again; whatever followed it in its exchange (its reply, a failed reply, or nothing) is SUPERSEDED, while a reply to an earlier message that was stored after it stays active, so retrying a failed regenerate repeats the same exchange. With `messageId` (an active assistant message): that response and every message after it are superseded, and the turn re-runs from the user message it answered. Superseded messages are kept in the message list and on disk, flagged as retained history, never deleted. Returns the superseded message ids so the caller can render the honest lineage. Rejected on a closed session (409 SESSION_CLOSED) or unknown session (404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND); a `messageId` that is unknown is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND, already superseded 409 MESSAGE_SUPERSEDED, not an assistant message 400 NOT_AN_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE; with no user message to answer again it is 409 NO_ANCHOR_MESSAGE. While a reply is streaming, a message is being prepared, or sends are queued it is refused with 409 CHAT_TURN_BUSY and nothing changes: stop the reply (or let it and the queue finish), then retry.

get.description: Find companion-chat messages whose text contains `query` (case-insensitive) across every chat, newest first. Each item names the chat (`sessionId`, `sessionTitle`), the message (`messageId`, `role`), a snippet around the match and `createdAt`. History retained behind a regenerate or edit is not searched. Closed chats are searched only with `includeClosed`. Paged: `limit` 1-100 (default 25); pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` while `hasMore` is true. A blank query is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT; a cursor this search did not return is 400 INVALID_CURSOR.

post.description: Send a message that runs IMMEDIATELY, interrupting the in-flight turn if one is running. The message jumps to the front of the pending-turn queue; the active turn is cancelled through the same finalization path as companion.chat.turns.cancel (any non-empty partial reply is persisted with `deliveryState: "cancelled"` and the terminal `turn.cancelled` event reaches every subscriber), then the steered message's turn starts. Messages queued behind an active turn keep their places behind the steer. With no turn running this behaves as an ordinary send. Accepts the same payload as companion.chat.messages.create (`body`/`content`, `attachments`, `metadata`). Returns the new message id, `steered: true`, and `cancelledTurnId` when a turn was interrupted. Ordinary sends posted while a turn is running are QUEUED (transcript-visible immediately with `deliveryState: "queued"`, answered in order), steer is the explicit jump-the-line verb. A queued message whose turn can never run (the chat closed, the service shut down or the daemon restarted first) ends as `deliveryState: "unanswered"`, never silently dropped.

delete.summary: Remove a Queued Companion Chat Message
delete.description: Take a companion chat message out of the queue before its turn starts, so it is never answered. The transcript keeps it, marked `deliveryState: "unanswered"`, and leaves it out of what the model sees. A message whose turn has started (or that was already removed) is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_QUEUED.

post.summary: Edit a Queued Companion Chat Message
post.description: Replace the text of a companion chat message still waiting for its turn; its attachments stay. The transcript shows the new text. A message whose turn has started (or that was removed) is 404 MESSAGE_NOT_QUEUED.

get.description: The messages of a companion chat waiting behind the running reply (sent while it was still being written), in the order they will be answered. Each stays editable and removable until its turn starts; a message whose turn has started no longer appears. An unknown chat is 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND.

post.description: Close a companion-chat session (soft close). The session record and its messages are preserved in closed state and remain listable with includeClosed. Distinct from companion.chat.sessions.delete, which permanently removes the record.

Create a new companion-chat session. Optional `provider` / `model` override the registry default. The session retains its requested `reasoningEffort`; null restores provider defaults. Title and system prompt are stored on the session record.

get.description: List active companion-chat sessions. Pass `includeClosed` to include recently closed sessions. Each record carries its title and system prompt, so it needs read:transcripts.

delete.description: Permanently remove a companion-chat session: the on-disk record file is deleted and the session is dropped from the shared session store, this does NOT merely close it (use companion.chat.sessions.close for a soft close). Requires the session to already be closed: deleting a still-active session is rejected with 409 SESSION_ACTIVE (close it, then delete). An unknown or already-deleted id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, never a 200-noop.

get.description: Return a companion-chat session record together with its full message history.

patch.description: Update companion-chat session metadata, including session-local provider, model and requested reasoning effort, without changing the daemon/TUI current model. Routing changes are refused while a reply is active; null effort restores provider defaults.

post.description: Open a closed companion-chat session again so it accepts messages. The model history is rebuilt from the saved transcript on the next send. A chat that is already open answers `reopened: false` with its current status; an unknown id is a 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND.

Stop the in-flight turn for a companion chat session, a true server-side stop: the provider stream is aborted, any non-empty partial reply is persisted to the transcript with an explicit `deliveryState: "cancelled"` marker (an honest partial, never disguised as a complete reply) AND committed to the model-facing conversation history with an explicit interruption note, later turns can reason about what the user saw and stopped, which is usually what a follow-up or steer refers to, and the terminal `turn.cancelled` event is published to every subscriber of the session stream so a stop from one client converges on all others. Any announced tool call without a result is closed with a synthetic error `turn.tool_result` before the terminal event. Optional `turnId` guards against cancelling a newer turn a stale stop raced against (409 TURN_MISMATCH). No turn in flight is the benign 404 NO_ACTIVE_TURN (the turn finished before the stop landed). When the turn has not stopped within 3 seconds (a tool call or the provider has not ended yet) the stop is still accepted and the answer is 409 TURN_STOPPING with `state: "stopping"`: treat the turn as stopping, not failed; the terminal `turn.cancelled` event follows when it stops. Repeat cancels are idempotent successes. The session stays open; the next message starts a fresh turn normally.

get.description: Return the resolved GoodVibes config snapshot.

post.description: Write one config value on the daemon: `{ key, value }`, where value is any JSON the key accepts. The response reports the value the host now holds and which file and tier it is in; a value that did not take is refused with what the host holds instead. A key that holds a credential takes only a goodvibes://secrets/ reference (store the secret with credentials.set); runtime.workingDir is saved and the daemon moves there in the same process once no session is mid-turn (every service starts again on the new directory and attached apps reconnect; `moving`, `waitingForSessions` and `note` say what happens, and a second change while it moves is 409 WORKSPACE_BUSY), or, on a host that cannot move, at its next start (`restartRequired`). The same route also serves the settings clients' lanes, which answer with that lane's own object: `{ settingsPrecondition }` takes action `capture` (read the facts a change would act on) or `write` (make it, optionally only while `ifServing` and `ifIncarnation` still hold; a repeated `requestId` returns the first answer), and `{ settingsImportPrecondition }` takes the same two actions plus `apply`, which spends a captured `reference`.

Remove the explicit value of one config key through the daemon API so it reads as its default again, in every settings file that holds it. The response reports the value the host now holds and which file and tier it came from. Refuses a key that holds a credential (use credentials.delete), a key the host does not know, a key locked by managed policy, and runtime.workingDir (change the workspace with config.set).

Write several config values on the daemon as one update: `{ entries: [{ key, value }] }`. Every entry is admitted before anything is written, each settings file is written once and the configuration revision moves once, so a pair of settings that only make sense together never lands half-applied. A refusal names the setting, the reason and the next step, and says what was saved (nothing, unless a later settings file could not be written after an earlier one was). The answer lists, per key, the value the host now holds and which file and tier it is in; when a key does not hold the value asked for (a higher tier overrides it, or it was coerced), the answer is 409 CONFIG_SET_NOT_APPLIED naming those keys in `notApplied`, with the revision written and every entry's held value. A key that holds a credential takes only a goodvibes://secrets/ reference; runtime.workingDir is set on its own with config.set.

Returns at once with the new contract and its owner agent id; the contract shapes, plans and runs on its own, and its progress arrives on the `contracts` event domain. When `sessionId` names a live session this daemon hosts, the contract starts in that session (origin `hosted`): its turns receive the contract's questions and a following turn answers them. Otherwise it starts on the daemon's own runner (origin `external`) under `sessionId`, or the `operator` session when none is given, in `workspaceRoot` (absolute), or the daemon's working directory. `isolation` overrides `contract.isolation` for this contract. 400 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when `ask` is empty, `workspaceRoot` is relative or outside the daemon's workspace, or differs from the hosted session's; 403 with SESSION_NOT_OWNED when the session belongs to another caller; 409 with SESSION_NOT_LIVE when `sessionId` names a hosted session that is no longer live.

Replay key: request header `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the first contract (with the Idempotent-Replayed: true response header) instead of starting a second one; the same key with a different body is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. Keys are kept with the contract store per caller, so a retry after a daemon restart still returns the first contract; the body is compared field by field, in any order. The key may also be sent as `idempotencyKey` in the body; the header wins when both are given. A replayed result carries `replayed: true`.

Without the flag no receipts are returned or marked, so identity probes and keepalives never take them.

get.description: Return inbox message summaries fetched live from the configured IMAP account, newest first (ordered by server-assigned UID, never by the sender-written Date header). Read-only (EXAMINE / BODY.PEEK); never marks messages read. `before` pages backwards: pass the smallest UID of the page you have to get the next older page; `total` counts every match. When the server answered for a message and the daemon could not read the answer, the page is short and `unreadable` says so, an omitted message is not by itself evidence that it was deleted. A message the daemon's inbox mirror has labelled carries `triageLabel` (spam, priority or normal); one not labelled yet has none. A message the mirror holds carries `screening`: `screened`, or `not-screened` when only code checked it for credential and card text, with `screeningReason`.
Return the full body and attachment metadata for a single inbox message by IMAP UID. Read-only (BODY.PEEK; does not mark as read).

post.description: Send a composed email via the configured SMTP account. Irreversible external send; requires confirm: true and explicit user review of recipients and body. Pass a clientSendId (8-128 letters, digits, - or _) chosen when the message was composed: a repeat with the same id and the same message within ten minutes returns the first answer instead of sending again (the id also becomes the Message-ID), and the same id with a different message is refused (409 CLIENT_SEND_ID_REUSED). A send whose final server reply was lost fails with EMAIL_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED: it may have gone, and repeating it with the same id will not send it twice.

get.description: The dependency-graph view of one workstream: nodes (id, title, state, cluster, files, merge state, blocked reason, orphaned flag, deepest-remaining-path depth, stalled tell, agent), edges (from depends on to), and the elastic-pool state (ready/running counts, at-cap, cap key + size, any spawn refusal). Surfaces render the task graph under the chain from this, the fleet/observability idiom. 404 when the workstream is unknown to this daemon.
Return the health integration snapshot.

The MemoryGovernor snapshot: the current memory-pressure tier and budget, resident set size and heap, the tier thresholds and hard limit in force, per-cache footprints the governor can shrink, which deferrable background jobs are paused, and the leak-tripwire state. When memory.budgetMb, memory.tier.* or memory.hardLimitPct were refused, `configFallback` names the settings and why; the shipped values shown are in force until the setting is fixed and the daemon restarts. Read-only observability so operators can see the daemon shedding memory before it approaches OOM.

post.description: Turn the owner keep-awake toggle on or off: a daemon-held sleep inhibitor INDEPENDENT of work state, surviving surface closes, persisted as power.keepAwake. Covers idle + sleep + lid-switch classes where grantable; the returned state names any refused class honestly. No timers, no AC-only sub-options, the always-visible chip is the safety mechanism. Emits runtime.ops OPS_POWER_STATE_CHANGED so every attached surface updates its chip.

get.description: The host sleep-ownership state: whether the automatic work inhibitor is held (and the live "held because X" reasons, cap, and expiry), and the owner keep-awake toggle with the classes the OS actually granted vs refused, a refused lid-switch block is stated honestly ("idle sleep blocked; lid-close suspend is controlled by your OS here"), never papered over. sleepEdge says whether work is checkpointed before sleep and caught up on wake, and its note says why not when it cannot be. Surfaces render the always-visible "sleep disabled" chip from this state and the runtime.ops OPS_POWER_STATE_CHANGED event.

What the daemon's runtime store holds now, by domain (session, conversation, agents, tasks, permissions and the rest), for debugging. domains names the ones to read, comma-separated; without it every domain is read, and available lists them all. The data is made safe on the way out: dates are ISO text, errors { name, message }, binary data "<N bytes>"; credential fields read [REDACTED] and owner-profile fields [REDACTED_PROFILE], and credential-shaped text is masked; nesting and total size are bounded, a cut value reads "[Truncated]" and truncated is true. unknown lists asked-for domains the store does not hold. Read-only.

post.description: Starts the one-act setup and answers at once with the run it started (or the run already in progress it joined); the install runs on in the daemon, voice.local.status serves its live progress as installInProgress and, when it ends, its receipt as lastInstall. The setup: download + checksum-verify the piper TTS engine, a default voice, and (where a pinned goodvibes-built bundle exists) the whisper.cpp STT engine with its default model into the goodvibes-managed directory, then point the voice.local.* config keys at the managed install, never overwriting a key you already set to a custom value (skipped keys are reported). The install ends by speaking a test phrase and reading it back: the transcript is compared word by word in code, allowing one differing word, and the receipt carries the transcript and the comparison. Downloads only when you ask; a failed or checksum-mismatched download keeps nothing.

get.description: Whether the managed local voice runtime (piper TTS + a default voice) is installed: not-provisioned (with a size-labeled offer), partial, provisioned, or unsupported-platform. STT (whisper.cpp) reports its own managed state: goodvibes builds and pins the whisper.cpp bundle per platform (no official prebuilt exists; provisioning never compiles on your machine), so where a pinned bundle exists STT provisions like TTS, and elsewhere it reports unsupported honestly. While a voice.local.install run is active, the response also carries installInProgress, the live per-component progress (phase, byte sizes where known) of that run, so surfaces poll this read during the install to render real progress; the section is absent when no install is running. Once a run ends, lastInstall carries its receipt (or the reason it stopped without one) with the run's start and finish times; a surface that started an install reads its result here. Read-only.

post.description: Sets voice up for what was asked: intent wake (this surface listens for the wake word; implies speech-to-text), stt, tts or voice (all of it), for the surface named (tui, agent, webui, app), which is the one that ends up listening. The plan is decided from this host's own facts (wake rows, wake models on disk, the managed speech runtimes, the input device); steps that need no answer are done at once (the wake rows are set, missing wake models are fetched), and the answer lists each step: do (done, or why it could not be), propose (acceptProposals: true does it) and ask (ttsChoice answers the text-to-speech question: local or a cloud provider this host holds a credential for). An install the plan needs is started and not waited for: installStarted names the run, and voice.local.status serves its progress and receipt. rendered is the plan as one reply a surface prints as-is; complete is true when nothing is left to answer and every step that ran finished.

get.description: Read one provisioned wake artifact in bounded chunks, for a surface that cannot fetch it itself, a browser tab, whose cross-origin fetch of the release asset is refused because that asset answers with no CORS header. Each chunk carries the offset, the whole artifact's size, and its PINNED sha256, so a client reassembles the file and verifies it against the pin: a truncated transfer fails at the consumer instead of loading as a model that silently never detects. Both classifier formats are served, "classifier" is the onnx build a browser tab loads, "tflite" the same classifier for a runtime that cannot, as is the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs ("vad"), and so is the attribution NOTICE of each redistributable artifact ("notice" for the classifier, "embedding-notice" for the front end, "vad-notice" for the gate), because a client that can fetch the bytes but not the NOTICE cannot satisfy the terms it received them under. Serves what is on disk and does not download; installation puts it there, and voice.wake.provision is the recovery path when it is missing.

post.description: Download and checksum-verify the pinned wake-word classifier in both runtime formats (onnx and tflite), the speech-embedding front end, the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs, and the attribution NOTICE of each, into the goodvibes-managed directory, about 6.1 MB. Installing goodvibes already does this, and a daemon retries at boot, so this verb is the RECOVERY path: an install that was offline, an artifact that failed verification, or a re-provision after the pinned model changes. Resumable by re-running: an artifact that already matches its pin is skipped, and one that is present but fails verification is replaced rather than used. A failed or mismatched download keeps nothing at the destination. Single-flight: two surfaces asking at once, or a boot attempt and a user asking, join one download instead of racing for the same files.

get.description: Whether the pinned wake-word artifacts are on disk and VERIFIED BY CONTENT: the "hey goodvibes" classifier, the tflite form of the same classifier, the speech-embedding front end the classifier sits behind, the speech gate voice.wake.vadThreshold runs, and the attribution NOTICE belonging to each of the three redistributable artifacts (the classifier's, the front end's and the gate's). Each reports verified, corrupt (present but failing its checksum, a truncated or swapped file, distinct from missing) and its byte size, with the total a fresh provision would download. Installing goodvibes provisions these, and a daemon retries at boot whatever the install could not fetch, so on a normal machine this reads ready without anyone having run a setup command; an offline install reports not-provisioned here until it is retried. The overall ready flag covers the classifier, the front end and both of THEIR NOTICEs, an artifact whose attribution is missing is not one this daemon may serve, and excludes two things: the tflite twin, which nothing here loads, so a host missing just that can still detect; and the speech gate, reported as vadReady instead, because voice.wake.vadThreshold defaults to 0 and the detector runs without it. Also restates that the model's published recall figures are measured on synthesised speech only, which any surface describing the model must carry. Never downloads. Read-only.
