post.description: Set the active default memory embedding provider.

get.description: Return one standing record's projection by id: its metadata entry plus the exact markdown the file projection would write (front-matter + content, with the live temporal status labelled). Returns 404 when no standing (project/team) record has that id, a session-scope or unknown id is an honest miss, never an empty projection.

Return the live projection of standing (project/team-scope) memory records, one metadata entry per record (id, filename, scope, class, summary, tags, confidence, review state, temporal validity + status), oldest first. This is the read view over the same standing memory the file projection writes as markdown; session-scope records are excluded (they are not standing memory). Computed live from the store, never read from disk, so it always matches the current records. An expired record is present with status:"expired" rather than silently dropped.

post.description: Add a memory record to the daemon-owned canonical store. The daemon is the single writer for its store; a client surface routes its writes here instead of opening the store file, so two processes never write the same sql.js file. New records default to confidence 60 (the recall floor) and reviewState fresh unless the review block overrides them. An optional caller-generated id (mem_<base36 time>_<8 hex>) makes the add safe to resend: the same id with the same record returns the stored row, the same id with a different record is refused.

delete.description: Permanently delete a memory record and its links from the canonical store. Delete means delete: the record is removed from the store and the semantic index, not merely flagged. Returns { deleted: false } when no record with that id existed, an honest boolean, never a 200 that pretends a phantom row was removed.

get.description: Return a single memory record by id from the canonical store, or 404 when no record with that id exists.

post.description: Export a no-loss bundle (records + links) for the given filter from the canonical store. The bundle round-trips through import id-keyed, so it is the wire form of the cross-surface fold/reconcile seam. Read-only.

Import a bundle into the canonical store as an id-keyed union: an id already present is left untouched (counted skipped), a new id is added; a link is added only when both its endpoints exist. Never overwrites, never deletes, idempotent on re-run. The daemon is the single writer, so a client imports here instead of writing the store file.

Create a directed relation (e.g. "supersedes", "caused") from the path record to a target record. Returns 404 when either endpoint does not exist, never a 200 that pretends a link was made between records that do not both exist.

get.description: Return every link where the record is the source or the target. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists, an honest not-found, distinct from a record that exists but has no links (an empty array).

post.description: Bulk read from the canonical store: a literal (non-semantic) search returning the matching records as a plain array. An empty filter returns every record (getAll). This is the read a client surface uses instead of opening the store file for its browse/list and knowledge-injection paths.

Search the canonical store, literal or semantic. When semantic is requested but the semantic index cannot be consulted, the search falls back to a literal scan and states the reason in indexUnavailableReason rather than returning a silent empty result that reads as "nothing was ever stored". With recall=true the cross-surface recall-honesty contract is applied: flagged (stale/contradicted) records are excluded outright and records below the 60% confidence floor are dropped, each exclusion counted honestly.

Rank records by semantic similarity against the query, returning scored results (distance, similarity, score). When the query has no vector match the store falls back to a lexical ranking rather than a silent empty. distance is null for a fallback (non-vector) result. Read-only against the daemon's canonical index.

Edit a record's content fields (scope, summary, detail, tags) and its temporal validity window (validFrom, validUntil) in the canonical store. This is distinct from the review update: it changes the record itself, e.g. moving scope project→team promotes a record to the shared surface. For validFrom/validUntil a number sets the bound, null clears it, and an omitted field leaves it unchanged, so a proposal that changes only the window can be applied. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists.

Update a record's review signal (reviewState, confidence, reviewer, staleReason) in the canonical store. Marking a record stale or contradicted flags it so the recall-honesty contract will never inject it into a prompt again regardless of confidence. Returns 404 when no record with that id exists.

get.description: Return memory records prioritised for review. Accepts optional limit (?limit=N) and scope filter (?scope=session|project|team). A scope query parameter that is present but not one of the three valid values returns 400.

The memory store's point-in-time copies, newest first: the daily copy, the copy taken before a schema migration, the copy every restore takes of the records it replaced, and the tripwire copy. Each with its name (what memory.snapshots.restore takes), why it was taken, when, its size on disk and how many records it holds (null when the copy could not be read). Only the records store is copied; the semantic index is rebuilt from the records. Empty for a store that lives in memory only.

post.description: Replace every memory record, link, consolidation proposal and store fact with those of one copy (its exact name from memory.snapshots.list, `latest`, or the start of one name such as a date). The owner's act only: requires confirm: true on an explicit request from the owner's own session, device or machine; an agent is refused. A copy of the records being replaced is taken first and named in `undoSnapshot`, so restoring it undoes this restore. One SQLite write transaction: processes that share the store (terminal app, Agent, daemon) see the restored records on their next read, and a failure part way leaves the store as it was. The semantic index then re-embeds only records whose text differs from what it holds (`vectorIndex: updating`). Answers which copy, records before and after, and links after.

x-error-codes.meaning: This store keeps no copies (an in-memory store), or a copy of the current records could not be taken first; nothing was changed.
No copy has that name (or there are no copies yet); nothing was changed.
More than one copy starts with that text; name one in full. Nothing was changed.
The copy cannot be read or was written by a newer version; nothing was changed.

post.description: Rebuild the sqlite-vec vector index.

get.description: Return the current sqlite-vec vector-store posture.

post.description: Record that the owner has one occurrence in hand, so nothing is pushed at them about it again. This is not a yes and not a no: the open item STAYS OPEN and stays enumerable, so occasions.pending still lists it, under acknowledged[] rather than in the nudge, and asking what is coming up still answers with it. Only the push stops. The record expires with its occurrence, so next year asks fresh. An occurrence already answered yes or no is left as it is: changed is false and reply says so. source names how it was recorded: conversation when the owner said so in a reply, explicit when a surface offered the action, gift-flow when the owner is already answering gift questions about it.

Record yes, no, later or acknowledged for one occurrence. A no goes silent for the rest of this cycle and expires with the date, so next year asks fresh carrying no memory of the refusal. A later is NOT a decline, it comes back roughly halfway to the date. A yes on a gift-giving occasion opens the short interview and returns its first question. A yes or a no RESOLVES the open item and removes it. A later keeps the item open and moves it to its return date with its pushes available again. An answer of acknowledged leaves the item standing and quiet (the same as occasions.acknowledge); on an occurrence already answered yes or no it changes nothing and ok is false with the reason.

Write the confirmed occasion as one line in the owner profile, under Important dates, carrying its provenance. self:true marks the owner's own date (written as for me), so a remember-only one is never pushed at them. This is the ONE confirmation: nothing re-confirms at nudge time, because for an annual date a silent write means the mistake surfaces up to eleven months later. Refused without a kind rather than defaulting one. Goes through the owner-profile write gate, so authority, surface and a verbatim quote of what the owner said are all required.

self.description: True when the date is the owner's own (their birthday). Written as `for me`; a remember-only date of the owner's is kept and listed but never pushed at them.

post.description: Apply the owner's answer to "which date is right?": keep names the date to keep, the other lines for that title are removed from the owner profile through the profile write gate (so authority is required with keep), answers and gift history stay, and the conflict is not raised again. Without keep nothing changes and dates lists what is recorded, to put to the owner. A conflict is never resolved automatically: only the owner knows which date was right. When the file already holds one date (the owner fixed it by hand) the reminder is closed and resolved is true.

keep.description: The date to keep, as recorded (MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to get the recorded dates back without changing anything.

post.description: Return what the owner landed on for one occasion in previous years, newest first. Kept beyond the answers deliberately: the answers expire with their date so next year asks fresh, the history does not.

Record one answer and return the next question, if there is one. The interview guides the owner to their own idea and never recommends a gift, that judgement is the owner's, which is also why the outcome recorded is what the owner landed on rather than what was suggested.

Return one gift interview and the question that has not been answered yet. A thread the owner walked away from resumes here rather than restarting: the next step is the one the owner did not get to. Over a channel the steps are asked one at a time; in the agent they can be one exchange.

post.summary: Record What The Owner Landed On
post.description: Close the interview with what the owner settled on and write it to the gift history. Recording the outcome rather than merely that the owner said yes is the point: "said yes in 2026" cannot stop year three steering where year one did.

get.description: Return every occasion declared in the owner profile, with its next occurrence, how many days away it is, the lead it uses, whether it is inside its lead window, and what was answered for that occurrence. Also returns lines under the heading that could not be typed, each with the reason, and any occasion that has two different dates recorded. This carries the dates: it is the owner asking their own system what it holds, which is the explicit ask that unlocks a closed-tier read. A nudge never does.

Return everything unresolved, without delivering anything: the batched nudge, any date conflict still open, and any interview left mid-thread. This is how a surface that is not a push destination receives a nudge, it pulls at the start of a turn rather than being pushed at, and a stored date is the prior scheduling that permits raising something unprompted. A nudge a push has already landed on the agent is left out while the agent is a configured push destination, so the push and the pull cannot raise the same thing twice; an item no push has ever landed there is still returned, so a missing sender or a failed send loses nothing. An occurrence inside its window is listed even before any sweep has opened it, so a machine that was just started still answers. Composed in code, the same with or without a decision model. The nudge names the occasion and the person and NEVER the date: proximity is a word, not a count of days.

post.description: Write the confirmed plan as one line in the owner profile, under Plans, carrying its provenance and every entry of details (a confirmation number, flights and times, who is travelling), which occasions.plans.list returns in extras. Same one-confirmation rule and the same owner-profile write gate as an occasion.

details.description: Everything else the owner gave about the plan, one detail per entry: a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling, why. Stored on the line exactly; a detail the line cannot hold unchanged refuses the write.

get.description: Return every plan declared in the owner profile, a dated range with attributes, plus whichever one has the owner away today. Plans are ambient: they never prompt. They exist so the system knows not to suggest things into that window, and so a nudge that would land while the owner is abroad moves to the day before they leave.

post.description: Work out what would be written for a plan heard in conversation, and return the one-line confirmation. Writes nothing. Away is opt-in rather than assumed: "the kitchen is being redone, 3rd to the 10th" is a real dated range that is not the owner leaving the house.

details.description: Everything else the owner gave about the plan, one detail per entry: a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling, why. Stored on the line exactly; a detail the line cannot hold unchanged refuses the write.

post.description: Remove one plan from the owner profile, chosen by planId (its normalised title) and planFrom when two plans share a name. One confirmation: confirmed:false returns the sentence to put to the owner and removes nothing. Goes through the owner-profile write gate, so authority is required.

planFrom.description: The start date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the plan meant, needed only when two plans share a name.

post.description: Change one recorded plan in place, chosen by planId (its normalised title) and planFrom when two plans share a name: any of title, from, to, away, destination and details (details replaces the list); a field left out keeps its value. With confirmed:false nothing is written and proposal carries the exact line and the sentence to put to the owner; with confirmed:true the new line is written and the old one removed, through the owner-profile write gate (authority, surface and said required).

planFrom.description: The start date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the plan meant, needed only when two plans share a name.

details.description: Everything else the owner gave about the plan, one detail per entry: a confirmation number, a flight and its times, who is travelling, why. Stored on the line exactly; a detail the line cannot hold unchanged refuses the write.

post.description: Work out what would be written for a date heard in conversation, and return the one-line confirmation to put to the owner. WRITES NOTHING. When no kind was given, needsKind is true and the confirmation asks for it in the same breath, the kind is the owner's choice and is never inferred, because no rule that reads a label tells a birthday from a death anniversary. Any date already recorded for the same name that disagrees comes back in conflictsWith.

self.description: True when the date is the owner's own (their birthday). Written as `for me`; a remember-only date of the owner's is kept and listed but never pushed at them.

post.description: Remove one occasion and every record the machine kept against it, answers, gift history, open items, interviews and calendar mirrors. Takes exactly one confirmation: not unquestioned, and not an argument. People divorce and people die. A confirmed:false call returns the sentence to put to the owner and removes nothing.

get.description: What the machine-owned store is holding, counts of answers, gift records, open items, interviews and calendar mirrors, plus what the last housekeeping pass removed and why, and whether the file was found unreadable. Counts and reasons only: no answer, no gift and no date is returned, which is what makes this safe in a support bundle.

post.description: Run one pass immediately: reap expired and orphaned state, find the occasions entering their lead window, batch them into a single message, mirror to the calendar if that is on, and deliver. Delivery goes to every destination in occasions.nudgeChannel, a comma-separated list, so Telegram and the agent both get it, and each is attempted independently, with deliveries[] naming per destination what landed and what did not. Housekeeping runs first and unconditionally, so a machine with nudging turned off still reaps. Returns hold:"quiet-hours" or hold:"disabled" when it deliberately said nothing, nothing is dropped, it waits. It runs the same with or without a decision model; with decision models off, provenance:"classic" says who each date is about was taken from the line's own for-me marker only. A push a destination accepted is recorded as sent even if settings or the profile changed during the send, so it is not pushed again next pass.

Change one recorded occasion in place: any of date, kind, person, recurrence, leadDays (null returns to the default) and self; a field left out keeps its value. The occasion keeps its id, so its answers, gift history and calendar mirrors stay attached. A new title is accepted only when it names the same occasion (spelling or case); a different name is refused, add it as a new occasion and remove this one. With confirmed:false nothing is written and proposal carries the exact line and the sentence to put to the owner; with confirmed:true the new line is written and the old one removed, through the owner-profile write gate (authority, surface and said required). An occasion recorded with two dates is refused until occasions.conflict.resolve settles it.

self.description: True when the date is the owner's own (their birthday). Written as `for me`; a remember-only date of the owner's is kept and listed but never pushed at them.

get.description: Return integration panel descriptors.

post.description: Open a listed panel in the terminal session this process runs. Answers opened: true only when the view appeared; an id GET /api/panels does not list is refused with 404, and a listed panel this process has no terminal screen to show is refused with 409.

get.description: Today's spending pools: the daily item budget, the separate overage budget that covers only unavoidable charges (tax, mandatory fees, and the delivery option actually used), and the tolerance allowance. Each reports its limit, what today has spent, what purchases in flight are holding, and what is left. Includes the calendar day and the timezone it was computed in, the day resets at midnight in daemon.timezone, UTC when unset, and whether this node is the one currently allowed to spend. Each spend keeps the day it was made on, in the zone then in force, and counts until that day is over, so changing the timezone cannot hand back a spent budget.

message.description: Which store stopped, why, that nothing recorded was lost, and the step: restart the daemon.

post.description: Store a card. The number, expiry, CVV and cardholder name go to the daemon secret store, encrypted at rest, under keys derived from the config path; only the label, brand, last four digits, kind and declared issuer cap are kept as config. The response carries the metadata record and never echoes what was submitted, because an echo would be a read path and no read path exists. A virtual card with a hard issuer cap is the recommended configuration: it bounds what any leak could cost to one killable number, which a real card number does not.

get.description: Configured cards, as METADATA ONLY: id, label, brand, last four digits, whether it is a virtual or a real card, expiry month and year, and the issuer spend cap the owner declared for a virtual card (declared, unverifiable by us, and never treated as an enforcement layer of ours). materialComplete reports whether every required secret field is present without revealing any of them. The card number, expiry, CVV and cardholder name live in the daemon secret store and there is no method that returns them.

delete.description: Delete a card: its config metadata and every secret derived from its config path, reporting how many secret entries were cleared so a partial deletion is visible rather than silent. payments.defaultCardId is not cleared by a delete; payments.cards.list shows a stale id as empty, and every purchase must name its card anyway.

post.description: The owner approves one purchase in advance, out of band from the conversation that will run it: the merchant's registrable domain, the item, and the most it may cost. Optional unless payments.confirmEveryPurchase is on. The amount is read in the budget currency ("25" and "25.00" are the same amount) and an amount no purchase could match is refused before anything is recorded. Mints a persisted, single-use approval bound to those fields, expiring in five minutes; a matching payments.checkout.begin spends it, and it answers that purchase's approval window for a total up to its amount. Requires confirm: true and the explicit-user-request context, the same confirmation gate every destructive verb on this daemon uses; /payments approve and the web UI send both. The response never carries card material; this verb never touches a card at all.

post.summary: Buy What Is In This Checkout
post.description: Admit one checkout against an open browser page and return a durable accepted acknowledgement before its approval/veto wait. Supply a stable requestId saved before sending; after a lost response, query payments.purchase.status with that ID. Reusing an admitted ID never starts another execution, even with changed input. Inside the owner's limits no prior approval is needed; with payments.confirmEveryPurchase on, a begin must state requestedMax and spend a matching payments.checkout.approve. cardId may be omitted to pay with payments.defaultCardId, and merchantDiscovered is read as sent. A purchase the owner asked for now carries the explicit-user-request context; one a schedule or trigger starts names standingId (payments.standing.list) instead and is bound to that entry's item, shops and maximums. The daemon parses amounts, checks cart/merchant/taint/recurrence and budget, runs the shipping ladder and owner window, fills stored addresses/card and submits once. Accepted does not mean purchased. Status retains processing, refusal, cancellation, verification and uncertain-submission outcomes. Disconnecting the caller does not cancel the operation; stopping or shutdown drains its actual work. An uncertain merchant submission is never retried automatically.

cardId.description: A card id from payments.cards.list. Omitted, the purchase is paid with payments.defaultCardId.

standingId.description: For a purchase a schedule or trigger starts, with nobody asking in the moment: the id of the owner's standing authorisation from payments.standing.list. The item must be that entry's item and the merchant one of its shops; the purchase may come to at most the smaller of its per-purchase maximum and what is left of its period. Omit it for a purchase the owner asked for now.

requestedMax.description: Owner-requested maximum for the entire purchase, including tax, mandatory fees and delivery. Supply one non-negative decimal amount in the configured budget currency, such as 20.00, without grouping, currency symbols or prose. Precision must fit that currency. Exceeding it requires a new explicit approval; silence never raises it. Required while payments.confirmEveryPurchase is on: it is the amount the owner approved.

post.description: Approve an above-budget purchase or explicitly acknowledge an in-budget purchase using the exact live purchase and window references. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. The same inbox also consumes authenticated channel replies. A stale, answered or expired window refuses; this never submits directly or overrides budget, merchant, page or address checks.

Stop an admitted checkout using its exact purchaseId and operationId, or object to a live window using purchaseId and windowId. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. Stopping is a request, not proof that an order was undone; inspect final status and merchant history if submission may have begun. No automatic retry.

Refuse the pending purchase using the exact live purchase and window references. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. The same inbox also consumes authenticated channel replies. A stale, answered or expired window refuses; this never submits directly or overrides budget, merchant, page or address checks.

After inspecting the merchant’s order history, explicitly record whether this exact uncertain or unverified checkout placed an order. Requires current paired admin authority, write:payments, confirm: true and inspectedMerchantHistory: true. The saved finding cannot be changed by a retry. Settles only original purchase/budget bookkeeping after its actual executor has drained; never submits or resumes an order. Missing local receipts never imply no charge. A no-order finding releases an original unspent hold but never credits already committed spend.

Under payments.cvvHandling prompt, hand the card security code the owner typed to the one approved purchase waiting for it, by its exact purchaseId and windowId from payments.purchase.status. Requires an explicit owner action, confirm: true and current paired admin authority with write:payments. The code is used for that purchase's card entry and kept nowhere. A closed or replaced request refuses; this never submits directly or overrides any budget, merchant, page or address check.

code.description: The three or four digits of the card security code, typed by the owner for this one purchase. Never stored.

get.description: Read durable checkout operation status and actual live approval/veto windows, and any approved purchase waiting for its card security code (securityCodes, under payments.cvvHandling prompt). Optionally select one purchase, including after reconnect or restart. An accepted operation is not a completed purchase; uncertain submissions must be checked with the merchant and are never automatically retried. Reading does not extend a deadline or resume execution. One exception: an input a daemon restart cancelled while a surface in another process was answering it completes on that surface's `consumed:true` report. `agentId` names the agent the surface is running for this input: it binds the reply so a message that arrived over a channel gets its answer routed back to that conversation, the same binding the daemon makes for the executors it spawns itself. `surfaceInstance`, sent with `agentId`, names the surface process running that agent; it is kept in the input's `metadata.deliveringSurfaceInstance` (cleared by a report that names none), so a surface that restarted can fail the inputs a process that is gone was answering. `answer` (sent with `consumed:true`, optionally with `status`) is the output that agent finished with, the daemon writes it into the session and delivers it to the channel. `claim:true` is how a surface takes an input before it starts work on it: it succeeds for one caller only, for a `queued` input, or for a `delivered` one with no agent bound for at least two minutes (a claimant that died before starting it).
